finding: GitHub ACTION_REQUIRED reads failed, but the contract says a check that waits for a human reads running.
why: ACTION_REQUIRED waits for a person. ci-wait ends at once on failed, and GitLab manual reads running, so the forges disagree.
fix: Move ACTION_REQUIRED to the running side, and add a test row.

finding: When the first draft read fails, the body is written, the flag can be cleared, and the answer is still ok.
why: D-32 refuses a lost draft only when was_draft is true. A failed read gives unknown, so the restore is skipped: the hazard of PRD AC-064.
fix: Refuse before the write when the first read fails.

finding: The draft-lost contract says a retry can set the flag, but a retry cannot.
why: A retry reads the flag as off, so was_draft is false and the restore never runs. The port has no verb that sets Draft.
fix: Remove the retry claim, and name the exact human recovery in the refusal.
evidence: The change is open for review until a human or a retry sets it.

finding: An empty last read becomes status running when the budget ends, so the unreadable rule is bypassed.
why: With budget 0 or a small budget on a change whose reads give no status, the answer says the checks keep running, and there may be no checks.
fix: After the last read, refuse unreadable when the read gave no status.
evidence: if elapsed >= budget: break ... return ok(status="running", elapsed=elapsed, id=change, reason="budget exhausted; the checks keep running")

finding: The receipt recheck covers node text only, and D-29 and the contract read wider than the check.
why: block_text reads only text leaves. A write with the same text and another link target, node type or media id passes.
fix: State in D-29's follow-up and in the contract what the receipt covers, or widen the hash.

finding: The empty-text fix covers inline text only. An empty fenced code block still emits an empty text node.
why: adf.py builds codeBlock content with token.content.rstrip, which is an empty text for an empty fence. The same shape was removed for paragraphs.
fix: Emit empty content for an empty code block, with a test.

criterion: blast radius: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: description-put and attachment-put now need preview and a text-bound receipt, but the direct caller 0008 still states the old call.
why: 0008 Acceptance and its fake follow SDD section 3, which D-29 supersedes in a ledger the 0008 executor does not read. An unmodified 0008 builds a call the port refuses.
fix: Add one line to plan-s2 DECISIONS.md or to the 0008 contract, and anchor the IOU there.
evidence: build_preview must write the preview file, pass preview, and hash block_text from md-to-adf. The 0008 contract and its fake of SDD section 3 do not name this yet (decision D-29)

finding: The live check reads CI twice and expects the two reads to agree.
why: A pipeline that finishes between ci-status and ci-wait makes the assert fail on a healthy port.
fix: Accept any contract word from the second read, and compare only when the first read was final.
evidence: assert waited["ok"] and waited["status"] == (status["status"] if status["status"] in final else "running")

finding: The IOU for thread-list and auth-status names no consumer.
why: The wiring rule asks for an anchor that names the symbol. The anchor names the live test, the only caller.
fix: Anchor the IOU to a plan contract that calls the verbs, or remove the verbs.
evidence: is the only caller; no plan contract names them. The feature gate decides to keep or remove them

finding: The GitLab ci-wait final-word test checks only that the word is not running.
why: A wrong mapping such as skipped read as failed still passes.
fix: Parametrize the expected word and assert equality.

finding: The rejected-position rule rests on forge error strings the author wrote, and the live check never exercises it.
why: forge_round_trip.py has a real pull request but never posts to a line outside the diff.
fix: In the live check, post with and without require_inline on a line outside the diff, and assert both answers.
evidence: REJECTED = {"github": "gh: Validation Failed (HTTP 422): line must be part of the diff", ...

finding: No test shows md-to-adf gives the same block_text with and without figures for one text.
why: D-29 and the contract rest on this claim.
fix: Add one test on text that mixes paragraphs and a figure token.

finding: The test for a broken .claude.json also checks a Codex config source.
why: A failure points at one name but two behaviours.
fix: Move the Codex lines into their own test.

finding: The note type is a forge-specific word in a contract that says both forges answer the same keys.
why: A caller cannot branch on it across forges, and no downstream plan names the field.
fix: Remove type from the thread note answer, or define a closed word set.

finding: The attachment-delete answer holds filename null, and the contract does not say so.
why: The contract row lists filename with no null case.
fix: Document the null in the contract row.

finding: issue-get takes owner/name#7 for a GitHub key, but always answers key as the bare number.
why: A caller cannot pass the answer back without the repository, and the contract does not say so.
fix: Document that the answer key is the number.

finding: The require_inline rejection policy sits at two GitLab sites and in GitHub.
why: A change to the rule, such as the reason text, needs several edits.
fix: Give the refuse-or-fall-back step one helper.
evidence: if payload.get("require_inline"): raise Refusal("position-rejected", refusal.reason) from None

finding: The note-URL fallback expression is written 3 times.
why: A change to the anchor form needs 3 edits.
fix: Extract one helper and call it from the 3 sites.

finding: The number part of key is only checked for a leading dash, so the cross-repo guard can be bypassed.
why: A full issue URL has no # and reaches gh as the number. Whether gh prefers the URL's repository is unverified. An empty number also reaches gh.
fix: Refuse bad-payload unless the number is digits.

finding: _ci_word builds its table on every call and ends with a conditional that guards an empty word.
why: A reader must parse the tail to see the empty and the unknown case.
fix: Move the table to a constant, with an early return for an empty word.

finding: A self-hosted host such as gitlab-ee.corp.example no longer names the kind.
why: The new test needs the word as a whole dot-separated part, so such a host refuses no-forge where v1 found the kind.
fix: Split the host on dashes too.

criterion: Acceptance: Forge keeps v1 names and JSON answers, same on GitHub and GitLab
finding: thread-list now drops every discussion with no line, and note-list skips any note with a type, so a reply on a plain note is in neither.
why: On GitHub every plain comment is in note-list. The change has no ledger entry. GitLab's note type is inferred from its API: unverified live.
fix: Make note-list include those replies, and record the choice with a Supersedes line.
evidence: discussions = [item for item in ... if _on_a_line(item)]; if not (item.get("system") or item.get("type"))

finding: D-36 removes description_hash from the description-put answer but says Supersedes none, although D-18 chose to put it there.
why: A reader who follows the ledger gets two live, conflicting decisions.
fix: Record the supersede of D-18 in the ledger.
